provenance.item: AUMLOK X2 — the words, rebuilt from common everyday English

sources.name: EFF large wordlist
sources.role: THE SOURCE OF EVERY WORD. SOURCE=eff

sources.name: wordfreq
sources.role: FILTER ONLY under SOURCE=eff: it measures and records every shipped word zipf and contributes no words. The deviation from the EFF-plus-frequency rule is recorded in data/COMMON-WORDS-PROVENANCE.md: of 53 words a reviewer flagged, 31 entered through the frequency source, including every proper name and one non-word, and EFF admits none of them.

zipf.note: the measured English zipf of every shipped word, so the court re-checks the rule without the venv

provenance.method: candidate = every EFF word (SOURCE=eff: no other word enters), restricted to 3-9 lowercase letters. Then, in order: the HARD BLOCK, the named category drops, the PLEASANTNESS PASS in data/safety/pleasant-drop.json (its named judgment categories, then X2's own measured zipf >= 3.5 bar applied to the whole pool), the proper-name and place rule, and the retired v2 custody vocabulary. Every survivor is allocated to one theme: its own theme first, then the theme lexicon, then the shared stem, then the band whose bucket for that letter is thinnest. A theme/letter below 40 words falls back to words another band holds. Anchors are the six-letter survivors whose every letter has a bucket of at least 12 in all three bands. NOTHING IS ADDED TO REACH A COUNT.

fallbacks.note: The theme is a NUDGE, not a rule. Each band draws its own theme first; a letter too thin in that theme falls back to other pleasant common words. This block is the count of how often the nudge was overridden, published so a reviewer can see it rather than trust it.

properNames.rule: a dictionary name or brand word with no common lowercase dictionary entry; plus the curated places and common-surname words, which are dropped by name and without that guard, because a place or a surname reads as one whatever else the dictionary says about the spelling (manila, smith)

pleasantness.kind: a CURATED JUDGMENT LIST with named categories, written for this repository. It is NOT a published source and the file says so about itself, so nobody mistakes it for one.

measuredTail.name: unfamiliar-tail
measuredTail.why: X2's own bar. X2 says: `PLUS a frequency list for breadth (keep words with English zipf frequency >= 3.5)`. In the EFF-alone rebuild that bar was applied only to the frequency source, so the EFF source admitted its whole tail: MEASURED, 62.1% of the shipped pool sat below it, and every word the coordinator flagged — direness, corroding, pungent, seduce, travesty, epidermis, delouse, outhouse, hemlock, batboy, snowiness, pettiness, rocklike, superjet, eastcoast, tipoff, unglue — lives in that tail. This pass applies X2's own number to the whole pool, uniformly.
measuredTail.note: X2's own number, applied to the whole pool instead of only to the frequency source. It is a MEASUREMENT and is recorded as one; the named categories above are the judgment.

measurement.note: NO BIT TARGET. X2 retired the 60/64-bit floor: reaching it forced ~500 words per letter per theme, which walked the harvest into the obscure tail and shipped an ethnic slur. This figure is measured from the data as written and compared to nothing.
